translationRepairs: In the early Tonghe reign he earned the jinshi degree and was appointed a patrol officer in Lulong.
In the early Huitong reign he earned the jinshi degree and was appointed a patrol officer in Lulong.
Chinese 會同初 names the Huitong reign; Tonghe (統和) is a different later era, and the following Taizong/Tianlu sequence confirms Huitong.
At the beginning of Tonghe he passed the jinshi examination and became a patrol officer in Lulong.
At the beginning of Huitong he passed the jinshi examination and became a patrol officer in Lulong.
Chinese 會同 must be Huitong, not Tonghe (統和); the literal field repeats the same era error as the idiomatic.
The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat.
The emperor mourned him deeply, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Chinese 贈尚書令 is a posthumous Shangshu ling appointment; Grand Preceptor would be 太師, so Director of the Imperial Secretariat is the correct office.
The emperor sighed in grief, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Grand Preceptor of the Secretariat.
The emperor sighed in grief, suspended court for two days, and posthumously appointed him Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
Chinese 尚書令 is not Grand Preceptor; correcting the literal title to Director of the Imperial Secretariat matches the source.
